blocks.text: Our Guide to Exterior Paint Maintenance for Your Townhome or Condo

If you own a condo or townhome in the Tacoma area, maintaining your exterior paint isn’t just about curb appeal, it’s about protecting your investment and staying compliant with COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA painting guidelines. Too often, owners wait until visible damage appears before addressing their exterior, which can lead to premature repainting, costly repairs, and friction with property management associations.

Whether you just had a fresh coat applied or you’re several years into your paint’s lifecycle, this guide will walk you through everything you need to know about condo exterior paint maintenance and how Black Pearl Painters can help extend the life of your investment with ease.

blocks.text: Step-by-Step Exterior Paint Maintenance Plan
1. Annual Pressure Washing (Spring/Fall)
Dust, pollen, mildew, and bird droppings degrade paint. We recommend gentle power washing once or twice a year using eco-safe cleaners.
2. Inspect for Damage Every 6 Months
Walk around your property and check for:

items: Worn or faded spots from sun exposure

blocks.text: Tip: Focus on south- and west-facing walls, they get the most UV damage.
3. Perform Seasonal Touch-Ups
If your building’s color is fading unevenly or minor peeling is beginning, spot touch-ups with matching paint help avoid premature full repaints.
Black Pearl offers touch-up kits and scheduled visits for this exact purpose.
4. Maintain Trim and Accents
Doors, shutters, and railings often wear faster than siding. Repainting these accent areas when needed keeps the whole home looking fresh.
